entry.title: DeepWeave: Weaving Neural and Symbolic Evidence for ML-Based Network Intrusion Detection System
entry.summary:
Machine learning-based network intrusion detection systems can recognize complex traffic patterns, but often require substantial labelled attack data, degrade under deployment shift, and provide limited evidence for analysts. We present DeepWeave, a probabilistic neuro-symbolic Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) that makes logic an integral part of detection. DeepWeave automatically constructs and validates interpretable rules, represents neural predictions as probabilistic predicates, and reconciles both evidence sources through explicit coupling policies over packet-, flow-, and hybrid-views.

Source: arXiv Systems & Architecture (cs.OS, cs.AR, cs.NI, cs.PF) · Tags: #computer-architecture #kernel-os #cryptography #ml-theory

entry.title: How Much Can Tool Calls Reveal About You? Privacy Leakage from Tool-Call Traces
entry.summary:
Large language model (LLM)-based agents interact with external tools through protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), producing tool-call traces that may expose behavioral signals about users. In this work, we systematically study the risk of user-profile inference from MCP tool-call traces, where observers infer user attributes from protocol-valid tool interactions without access to user conversations. We introduce PrivacyTrace, a benchmark containing 1,000 synthetic user profiles and 4,000 agent trajectories across four domains, generated with real MCP tools from 25 servers.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #llm #agents

entry.title: From Training Exposure to Membership Evidence: A Controlled Study of OLMo 2
entry.summary:
Whether a language model was trained on a document matters for copyright, privacy, and benchmark contamination. Yet most membership-inference (MI) evaluations on language models collect members and non-members after the fact, so success may reflect distribution shift and failure is inconclusive. We re-ran OLMo 2 1B's official 50-billion-token mid-training stage, replacing selected training chunks with documents from 7,814 pairs matched on domain and difficulty.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #llm #ml-theory

entry.title: PP-Mark: Provable and Publicly Verifiable Watermarking for Generative AI
entry.summary:
Generative AI models now produce images indistinguishable from real data, making publicly verifiable provenance essential; however, existing watermarking methods become vulnerable to forgeries and adversarial optimization attacks once their detectors are made public. We propose PP-Mark, a provenance framework that anchors lightweight statistical detection to a zero-knowledge proof of the embedding process, ensuring that forged content cannot pass full verification by construction. We establish formal unforgeability under standard cryptographic assumptions and validate PP-Mark against representative baselines across two latent-diffusion models (SD2.1 and SDXL), demonstrating resistance to black-box imprint forgery, white-box optimization, and regeneration attacks while remaining practical for decentralized verification.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics #clean-tech

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: Ideal Pseudorandom Code, Revisited
entry.summary:
Pseudorandom error-correcting codes (PRCs), introduced by Christ and Gunn at CRYPTO’24, combine pseudorandomness with error correction, providing a natural abstraction for robust watermarking and steganography on generative AI models. Subsequent standalone notions, which are ideal security for secret-key PRCs and CCA-style security for public-key PRCs, are oracle-based and do not capture composable use with explicit parties, sessions, and corruption. We give a UC treatment of PRCs via corruption-aware ideal functionalities for both settings.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: Low-Space Quantum Discrete Logarithms on Genus-Two Jacobians. Quantum discrete logarithms on genus-two Jacobians require reversible arithmetic with controlled workspace.
entry.summary:
Quantum discrete logarithms on genus-two Jacobians require reversible arithmetic with controlled workspace. Generic divisor-addition formulas apply only outside an exceptional set, which must be accounted for in quantum phase computation. We give a randomized reduction using two fresh independent uniform public seeds in a finite abelian group of odd order to randomize a complete balanced addition tree.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #number-theory #quantum-computing

entry.title: Threshold Post-Quantum E-Voting from Lattice Commitments
entry.summary:
Lattice-based homomorphic e-voting protocols built on commitments, such as EVOLVE, keep ballots private against all but one authority and the tally verifiable even if all authorities collude, but need every authority to tally. We present T-EVOLVE, in which votes are Shamir-shared over the commitment message space: any t of n authorities that took part in the checking phase complete the tally, privacy holds against t-1 colluding authorities and verifiability against all. The voter proves that her committed shares form a Reed-Solomon codeword whose value at zero is a valid vote; the parity checks cost no communication, and tallying interpolates public column sums without norm growth.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: Add/XNOR Chains: An NP-Complete Boolean-Arithmetic Problem at the Meet-in-the-Middle Barrier
entry.summary:
We introduce the Add/XNOR decision problem: given $n$ words of $n$ bits, decide whether they can be combined into zero by a left-associative chain in which each operator is either addition modulo $2^n$ or bitwise XNOR. We prove NP-completeness by a deterministic reduction from Subset-Sum{} in which four-bit guard fields and a parity normalization force every gadget to be all-additions or all-XNORs; hardness persists for every width that is a fixed rational power of the operand count, and 3-SAT reduces with linear parameter blow-up. The problem is a minimal model of Boolean--arithmetic mixing, and we give an exact theory of its linear and differential behaviour: a carry decomposition, closed forms for every single-bit linear correlation (for addition runs $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ the bit-$1$ correlation is $\prod_j2^{-z_j/2}\cos(z_j\pi/4)$, averaging exactly $(n+1)2^{-n}$), and an exact transposition differential with collision probability $2(5/8)^{m-1}-2^{-(m-1)}$, all confirmed experimentally.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
